[Country Sourdough Bread] ## Overview
A classic naturally leavened rustic country sourdough loaf with 75% hydration and 20% sourdough starter inoculate.

[Country Sourdough Bread] ## Ingredient Table
| Ingredient | Weight (g) | Baker's Percentage (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Bread Flour | 1000g | 100.0% |
| Water | 750g | 75.0% |
| Active Sourdough Starter | 200g | 20.0% |
| Fine Sea Salt | 20g | 2.0% |

[Country Sourdough Bread] ## Method & Fermentation Steps
1. Autolyse: Mix flour and 700g water; rest for 45 minutes at room temperature (78°F).
2. Inoculation & Salt: Add starter and remaining 50g water with fine sea salt. Mix thoroughly.
3. Bulk Fermentation: Perform 4 sets of stretch-and-folds spaced 30 minutes apart. Total bulk time: 4.5 hours.
4. Shaping: Preshape, bench rest 20 minutes, then final shape into a round banneton.
5. Cold Proof: Retard in refrigerator at 38°F for 14 hours.
6. Baking: Preheat Dutch oven to 450°F (230°C). Bake covered 20 mins, uncovered 22 mins.

[Country Sourdough Bread] ## Allergen Note
Contains Wheat (Gluten). Manufactured in a facility that handles nuts and sesame.

[Traditional Baechu Kimchi] ## Overview
A traditional Korean fermented cabbage dish salted with coarse salt, seasoned with gochugaru, garlic, ginger, and fermented at room temperature.

[Traditional Baechu Kimchi] ## Ingredient Table
| Ingredient | Weight (g) | Baker's Percentage (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Napa Cabbage | 2000g | 100.0% |
| Coarse Korean Sea Salt | 150g | 7.5% |
| Korean Chili Flakes (Gochugaru) | 80g | 4.0% |
| Garlic Cloves | 50g | 2.5% |
| Fresh Ginger | 20g | 1.0% |
| Fish Sauce (Anchovy) | 40g | 2.0% |
| Fermented Salted Shrimp (Saeujeot) | 25g | 1.25% |

[Traditional Baechu Kimchi] ## Method & Fermentation Steps
1. Salting: Quarter Napa cabbage, rub coarse sea salt between leaves, and soak in brine for 6 hours.
2. Rinsing: Rinse thoroughly 3 times with cold water to remove excess surface salt and drain for 2 hours.
3. Paste Preparation: Blend garlic, ginger, fish sauce, salted shrimp, and gochugaru into a thick seasoning paste.
4. Rubbing: Generously coat each leaf with seasoning paste.
5. Fermentation: Pack tightly into an airtight onggi or glass jar. Ferment at 65°F (18°C) for 3 days, then store at 36°F in refrigerator.

[Traditional Baechu Kimchi] ## Allergen Note
Contains Fish (Anchovy) and Crustacean Shellfish (Shrimp). Gluten-free.

[Primary Kombucha Fermentation] ## Overview
A tangy, effervescent fermented tea created via a symbiotic culture of bacteria and yeast (SCOBY) converting sucrose into organic acids.

[Primary Kombucha Fermentation] ## Ingredient Table
| Ingredient | Weight (g) | Baker's Percentage (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Filtered Spring Water | 3500g | 100.0% |
| Organic Cane Sugar | 250g | 7.14% |
| Black Tea Leaves (Assam) | 25g | 0.71% |
| Active Kombucha Starter Liquid | 350g | 10.0% |
| Mature SCOBY Pellicle | 150g | 4.28% |

[Primary Kombucha Fermentation] ## Method & Fermentation Steps
1. Tea Brew: Steep tea in 1000g boiling water for 15 minutes. Strain tea leaves.
2. Sugar Dissolution: Dissolve organic cane sugar in hot tea concentrate.
3. Dilution: Add remaining 2500g cold filtered water to bring brew temperature down below 80°F (27°C).
4. Inoculation: Pour active starter liquid and place SCOBY on top. Cover vessel with breathable cotton cloth and rubber band.
5. Primary Fermentation: Ferment undisturbed in darkness at 75°F–80°F (24°C–27°C) for 7 to 10 days until pH reaches 2.8 to 3.2.

[Primary Kombucha Fermentation] ## Allergen Note
Naturally gluten-free and vegan. Contains trace caffeine and residual ethanol (<0.5% ABV).

[Traditional Red Miso Paste (Akamiso)] ## Overview
A rich, deeply umami fermented soybean paste made from cooked soybeans, rice koji (*Aspergillus oryzae*), and sea salt aged for 6 to 12 months.

[Traditional Red Miso Paste (Akamiso)] ## Ingredient Table
| Ingredient | Weight (g) | Baker's Percentage (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Dried Soybeans | 500g | 100.0% |
| Rice Koji (Inoculated) | 500g | 100.0% |
| Non-Iodized Fine Sea Salt | 230g | 46.0% |
| Reserved Soybean Cooking Liquid | 150g | 30.0% |

[Traditional Red Miso Paste (Akamiso)] ## Method & Fermentation Steps
1. Soak & Boil: Soak dried soybeans for 18 hours. Simmer for 4 hours until beans can be crushed between thumb and pinky.
2. Mashing: Drain and reserve 150g liquid. Mash hot cooked soybeans into a smooth paste.
3. Mixing: Cool beans to 100°F (38°C). Mix with rice koji, sea salt, and reserved liquid until homogenous.
4. Packing: Form paste into balls and throw firmly into a ceramic crock to eliminate air pockets.
5. Salting Surface: Sprinkle 20g salt over the top surface, apply plastic wrap directly, and weight down with 2kg weights.
6. Aging: Ferment at room temperature in a dark pantry for 6 to 12 months.

[Traditional Red Miso Paste (Akamiso)] ## Allergen Note
Contains Soy. Gluten-free if rice koji is cultivated on 100% white rice.

[Naturally Fermented Garlic Dill Pickles] ## Overview
Crisp full-sour deli pickles fermented in a 3.5% sea salt brine with fresh dill heads, mustard seed, and oak leaves for natural tannin crunch.

[Naturally Fermented Garlic Dill Pickles] ## Ingredient Table
| Ingredient | Weight (g) | Baker's Percentage (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Kirby Pickling Cucumbers | 1000g | 100.0% |
| Filtered Water | 1000g | 100.0% |
| Non-Iodized Pickling Salt | 35g | 3.5% |
| Fresh Flowering Dill Heads | 20g | 2.0% |
| Garlic Cloves (Crushed) | 25g | 2.5% |
| Yellow Mustard Seeds | 5g | 0.5% |
| Black Peppercorns | 4g | 0.4% |
| Fresh Tannin Leaves (Oak/Grape) | 2 leaves | N/A |

[Naturally Fermented Garlic Dill Pickles] ## Method & Fermentation Steps
1. Cucumber Prep: Trim 1/16th inch blossom end off cucumbers (contains softening enzymes). Soak in ice water for 30 minutes.
2. Brine Creation: Whisk 35g pickling salt into 1000g cold filtered water until completely dissolved (3.5% brine).
3. Jar Packing: Layer garlic, dill heads, mustard seeds, peppercorns, and tannin leaves at the bottom of a wide-mouth jar. Pack cucumbers vertically as tightly as possible.
4. Submersion: Pour brine over cucumbers to submerge completely. Place a glass fermentation weight on top.
5. Fermentation Time: Ferment at 68°F–72°F (20°C–22°C) for 7 days (half-sour) or 14 to 21 days (full-sour).

[Naturally Fermented Garlic Dill Pickles] ## Allergen Note
Naturally gluten-free, nut-free, and vegan. Contains Mustard (Mustard Seeds).

[Lacto-Fermented Blueberries (Noma Style)] ## Overview
A modernist culinary technique using 2.0% salt by weight in a vacuum-sealed bag to create floral, effervescent, and savory-sweet lacto-fermented berries.

[Lacto-Fermented Blueberries (Noma Style)] ## Ingredient Table
| Ingredient | Weight (g) | Baker's Percentage (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh Organic Blueberries | 500g | 100.0% |
| Non-Iodized Fine Sea Salt | 10g | 2.0% |

[Lacto-Fermented Blueberries (Noma Style)] ## Method & Fermentation Steps
1. Weighing: Rinse and thoroughly dry blueberries. Weigh precisely on a digital scale (500g).
2. Salting: Calculate exactly 2.0% salt (10g). Toss blueberries with salt in a stainless steel bowl until berries are evenly frosted with salt crystals.
3. Vacuum Sealing: Transfer salted berries to a food-grade vacuum bag. Seal on full vacuum pressure without crushing berries.
4. Fermentation Window: Place bag flat in a dark incubator or room temperature spot (82°F / 28°C).
5. Monitoring: Over 4 to 5 days, the bag will inflate like a balloon from carbon dioxide production.
6. Finishing: Pierce bag, drain and reserve lacto-blueberry juice, store berries in an airtight jar refrigerated at 38°F.

[Lacto-Fermented Blueberries (Noma Style)] ## Allergen Note
Naturally vegan, dairy-free, nut-free, and gluten-free. No added preservatives.
